newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LILLE BEAT MARSEILLE IN DISPUTED TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LILLE BEAT MARSEILLE IN DISPUTED TIE.

text.p: Lille knocked former European champions Marseille out of the French Cup on Tuesday in a first round tie which should have been played two weeks ago.
Initially scheduled for January 20, the match was postponed after a legal battle between the two clubs over the venue.
The French Federation said Lille should host the match as Marseille's pitch could not be used because of work being carried out at the ground ahead of the 1998 World Cup.
A civil court then decided to postpone the match before a compromise led to it being played on a neutral ground in Valence, southeastern France.

Lille scored the game's only goal in the 33rd minute when Marseille goalkeeper Andreas Koepke turned a powerful shot by David Garcion on to the bar and Franck Renou headed in the rebound. Lille goalkeeper Jean-Marie Aubry made several fine saves to deny Marseille an equaliser.
Lille play host to Lyon in the second round on Saturday.
